27	    }

29	    def __init__(self, value, params):

124	
125	        self.__datetime = self.__datetime.replace(tzinfo=None)
126	        self.__datetime = pytz_timezone.localize(self.__datetime)
127	
128	        return self.__datetime
129

131	        dt = self.__datetime.utcoffset()
132	
133	        return int(

135	            + float(dt.seconds)

137	        )

content.text: This confirms it: the tests were updated to use `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo` (the modern stdlib replacement for `pytz`), but the converter code still calls the pytz-only `.localize()` method. This is a real bug — not flaky or obsolete tests. Skipping/deleting them would hide broken timezone conversion for anyone using `zoneinfo` (the standard approach in modern Python). The actual fix is small, so I'll just fix it properly rather than mask it.

content.text: Now let's confirm the full suite is green.

All 835 tests pass now.

The 5 failures were a real bug, not test flakiness: `typepy/converter/_datetime.py` called the pytz-only `.localize()` method on timezone objects, but the tests (and presumably real callers) pass `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo` instances, which don't have that method. Deleting or skipping those tests would have hidden broken timezone handling for anyone using the standard-library `zoneinfo` module. Instead I added a fallback in both call sites (`__from_datetime` and `__from_datetime_string`) that uses `.replace(tzinfo=...)` when the timezone object isn't a pytz-style zone with `.localize()`.

All 835 tests pass now.

The 5 failures were a real bug, not test flakiness: `typepy/converter/_datetime.py` called the pytz-only `.localize()` method on timezone objects, but the tests (and presumably real callers) pass `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo` instances, which don't have that method. Deleting or skipping those tests would have hidden broken timezone handling for anyone using the standard-library `zoneinfo` module. Instead I added a fallback in both call sites (`__from_datetime` and `__from_datetime_string`) that uses `.replace(tzinfo=...)` when the timezone object isn't a pytz-style zone with `.localize()`.
